## Summary

title: feat: add castellated holes to board outlines
description: Proposes an additive way to describe castellated holes directly in a board  outline.
body:
## Summary

Proposes an additive way to describe castellated holes directly in a `<board />` outline:

```tsx
<board
  outline={[
    { x: "-5mm", y: "-5mm" },
    {
      x: "-5mm",
      y: 0,
      isCastellatedHole: true,
      holeDiameter: "0.8mm",
      padDiameter: "1.2mm",
      connectsTo: "net.GND",
    },
    { x: "-5mm", y: "5mm" },
    { x: "5mm", y: "5mm" },
    { x: "5mm", y: "-5mm" },
  ]}
/>
```

Each flagged point is both an ordinary outline vertex and the center of the castellated hole. Existing `Point[]` outlines remain valid without migration.

## API decisions

- `isCastellatedHole` marks the outline point; its related geometry and connectivity props are flat on the same object.
- `holeDiameter` and `padDiameter` are required when `isCastellatedHole` is true, making the drill and copper dimensions explicit without manufacturing-sensitive defaults.
- `connectsTo` is optional and accepts one or more connection targets, also matching `<platedhole />`.
- Distance strings are normalized to millimeters by the existing distance parser.
- The type and schema are exported as `BoardOutlinePoint` and `boardOutlinePoint` for downstream consumers.

This PR is intentionally the props/API layer. Follow-up work in `circuit-json` and `core` will need to preserve the annotations in `pcb_board` output and materialize the fabrication/rendering behavior.

Related to tscircuit/tscircuit#3297.

## Testing

- `bun test`
- `bun run typecheck`
- `bun run build`
- `bun run check-circular-deps`
- `bun run format:check`
- required generated documentation scripts

## Summary

- map `schSize="sm"` and `schSize="xs"` to the premade compact passive symbols released in [`schematic-symbols@0.0.242`](https://github.com/tscircuit/schematic-symbols/pull/459)
- preserve the selected resistor style: the default IEC box uses `boxresistor_sm` / `boxresistor_xs`, while `symbolName="resistor"` uses the compact US zigzag family
- use `capacitor_sm` / `capacitor_xs` for non-polar capacitors while leaving polarized capacitors unchanged
- keep orientation suffixing centralized and fall back to the original symbol base when compact symbols are unavailable through an older wildcard peer dependency

## Behavior

| JSX | Selected symbol base |
| --- | --- |
| `<resistor schSize="sm" />` | `boxresistor_sm` |
| `<resistor schSize="xs" />` | `boxresistor_xs` |
| `<resistor symbolName="resistor" schSize="sm" />` | `resistor_sm` |
| `<resistor symbolName="resistor" schSize="xs" />` | `resistor_xs` |
| `<capacitor schSize="sm" />` | `capacitor_sm` |
| `<capacitor schSize="xs" />` | `capacitor_xs` |

`@tscircuit/props` already accepts `xs` and `sm` for resistor and capacitor `schSize`, so no props release is required. `default`, `md`, numeric distances, custom symbol names, and compact polarized capacitors retain their existing behavior in this change.

## Validation

title: fix: detect via copper overlapping pad corners
description: Fixes detection of via copper overlapping pad corners to ensure accurate placement error reporting.
body:
## Stacked PR

This fix is stacked on reproduction PR #242 and addresses #241. Its base is repro/issue-241-via-pad-corner-overlap, not main. Do not merge it independently of the reproduction boundary.

PR #242 uses Bun test.failing semantics so the known-bug assertion executes as an expected failure without making CI red. This PR explicitly converts that qualifier back to ordinary test(...) because the fix satisfies the assertion.

## Root cause and fix

checkViasInPads queried the spatial index at only the via center and then tested only whether that point was inside a pad. A via whose center was outside a rectangular pad could therefore be skipped even when its copper radius crossed an edge or corner.

The check now queries with the full via copper bounds and uses the existing shape-aware getPadToPadGap geometry. A gap at or below zero is contact/overlap; a positive gap remains clear. Existing board-level via-in-pad allowance and shared-layer filtering are unchanged.

The placement message now describes copper overlap instead of claiming the via center is inside the pad.

## Visual acceptance

The #242 snapshot changes from placement via/pad overlap errors: 0 to 1 and adds the rendered error text naming the via coordinates and R1.pin1.

## Verification

- Focused tests — 12 passed, 0 failed
- bun test — 187 passed, 0 failed
- bun run build — passed, including declaration generation
- Targeted Biome formatting and git diff --check — passed

description: Add compact passive symbol variants including small and extra-small box resistors, US resistors, and capacitors with various orientations and dimensions.
body:
## Summary

- add `sm` and `xs` box resistor, US resistor, and capacitor bases, each exported in right, left, up, and down orientations
- use common terminal spans of `0.50` for `sm` and `0.35` for `xs`
- preserve recognizable bodies and capacitor plates while removing proportionally more lead length
- reduce the US resistor zigzag from 8 geometry vertices in `sm` to 6 in `xs`, while preserving its `0.19` peak-to-peak height
- preserve capacitor `pos`/`neg` aliases, readable REF/VAL annotations, generated exports, and snapshots

## Geometry rationale

These are intentionally not uniform scales of the existing symbols. KiCad's [small US resistor](https://gitlab.com/kicad/libraries/kicad-symbols/-/blob/v9/Device.kicad_sym?ref_type=heads#L145378) reduces zigzag turns while retaining tooth amplitude, and compact Altium passives similarly concentrate their recognizable geometry in the body/plates with short external leads. The `0.50` small span also follows the historical maintainer sizing guidance in #276; `0.35` is a proportional extra-small step selected through shared-scale visual review.

The resulting right-facing geometry is:

| family | `sm` | `xs` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| box resistor | `0.35 × 0.15` body, `0.075` stems | `0.28 × 0.13` body, `0.035` stems |
| US resistor | `0.32 × 0.19` body, `0.09` stems | `0.23 × 0.19` body, `0.06` stems |
| capacitor | `0.32` plate height, `0.12` gap, `0.19` stems | `0.28` plate height, `0.10` gap, `0.125` stems |

- `bun test`

title: fix: preserve default platform config maps
description: Fixes the issue where custom project configurations could erase built-in footprint resolvers and other default settings, ensuring that defaults are preserved unless explicitly overridden by the project.
body:
## Summary

- deep-merge project platform-map overrides with the CLI defaults
- preserve built-in footprint resolvers, file parsers, static loaders, autorouters, and SPICE engines unless the project overrides the same key
- add regression coverage for the build pipeline's normalized, SPICE-only project config

## Root cause

The build worker first combines platform configs with `mergePlatformConfigs`. That helper materializes absent nested maps as `{}`. `getPlatformConfigWithCliDefaults` then shallow-spread the normalized project config over the default config, so an empty `footprintLibraryMap` erased the built-in `kicad` and `jlcpcb` resolvers.

This meant a project that only configured a custom `spiceEngineMap` could no longer load KiCad footprints. It surfaced as `No footprint resolver is configured for library "kicad"` in [this TI release build](https://tscircuit.com/tscircuit/ti/releases/c426ce29-c854-41fe-be28-3a835b67b418).

The fix reuses the existing map-aware merge helper with defaults first and project config second, so project entries still take precedence.

Companion cleanup for the three stale identifiers exposed after restoring the resolvers: tscircuit/ti#139.

## Testing

- `bun test tests/shared/get-platform-config-with-cli-defaults.test.ts`
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bun run format:check`
- `bun run build`
- related build-concurrency and static-file-loader tests

The regression first passes a SPICE-only config through `mergePlatformConfigs`, confirms the empty maps produced by that normalization step, and then verifies all CLI defaults survive.

## Summary

- preserve explicit `.ts`/`.tsx` imports during library transpilation by enabling TypeScript 5.7+ relative-extension rewriting
- retain the existing fallback for older TypeScript versions
- add a regression test covering a user tsconfig with `allowImportingTsExtensions`

## Cause

The transpiler unconditionally overrode `allowImportingTsExtensions` to `false` because plain TypeScript emit cannot use it. Projects such as `tscircuit/ti` intentionally import `.tsx` files and therefore produced TS5097 for every import during both ESM and CJS bundling. TypeScript 5.7 introduced `rewriteRelativeImportExtensions`, which makes this combination emit-safe.

Reproduction: https://tscircuit.com/tscircuit/ti/releases/1a2d8fe2-3a34-468a-9557-70d7102d837b

## Summary

- pin high-density-repair03 PR #82 so the connectivity map is authoritative when exact DRC resolves electrical nets
- add the complete nRF52810 Pipeline7 fixture plus the historical bad exact-geometry candidate
- assert that the fixed exact stage keeps the two real inherited issues, introduces neither the GND/VBAT contact nor the X1 via-pad violation, and emits no new post-power DRC identities

Pipeline7 exact DRC resolved a routed trace to a generated connectivity-net id but could resolve a connected raw PCB port to a point-pair alias. - add `ClockBuffer_LMK1C1104`, filling the `Clocks & timing` → `Clock buffers` category represented in `ti-sysblocks`
- add and export the LMK1C1104 TSSOP-8 chip model
- reproduce the functional drawing area of TI's LMK1C1104EVM Altium schematic with all 64 components, 160 ports, the input/power/output topology, Y0–Y7 validation fixtures, and the source's DNP population state

`OE` is the public API alias for TI's `1G` pin/net label because tscircuit net selectors cannot begin with a digit. The chip symbol still identifies the physical pin as `1G`.

Consumers can instantiate the subcircuit and connect through the exposed parent nets, for example `net.CLKIN`, `net.OE`, and `net.Y0`–`net.Y3`.

```sh
bun run scripts/convert-single-reference.ts HSDC078A_Validation_Board_Schematic.SchDoc schematic.circuit.json
```

The normalized conversion contains 917 Circuit JSON elements and validates cleanly. Altium stored 49 passive MPNs in `Comment` while hiding their electrical values in `Value`; normalization restored those resistor/capacitor values before validation.

Provenance hashes:

- `SNAR039.ZIP`: `2fd36888e5713ba79fe4f79e41332dc87eed296656d6cd5785cbf95bcabc4781`
- main `.SchDoc`: `787e4a3067ffd033d45af0b09c6bccdf704f1e3801d38eaa9f99ae3af644d761`
- normalized Circuit JSON: `4ed3e68e6e4558bf9fbf0a42ccd8b46ad63c5e0bc9d1ef2857f924933399a55c`

The Altium PCB document is an unsynchronized 16-pin LMK1C1108 validation layout. The schematic and BOM identify the actual LMK1C1104 as `PW0008A` TSSOP-8, so this implementation uses the correct 8-pin footprint and a newly routed PCB snapshot rather than claiming literal PCB reproduction.

## Validation

- `bun run typecheck`
- `bun run format:check`
- `bunx tsci build lib/subcircuits/ClockBuffer_LMK1C1104.circuit.tsx`
- `bunx tsci snapshot lib/subcircuits/ClockBuffer_LMK1C1104.circuit.tsx --test --concurrency 1`
- `git diff --check`
- nested-consumer audit of every exposed-net bridge
- root export/map smoke check
- Circuit JSON audit: 64 source/schematic/PCB components, 160 source/schematic/PCB ports, 114 source traces, 91 schematic traces, 106 PCB traces, 36 vias, 12 explicit nets, correct ground/power flags, and zero `*_error` records

The nested-consumer audit verifies parent connectivity for exactly `CLKIN`, `OE`, `VDD`, `GND`, and `Y0`–`Y3`, while Y4–Y7 remain scoped to their DNP fixtures.

The build succeeds. Its remaining placement warnings come from retaining TI's tightly packed validation-fixture geometry; supplier-footprint IoU and unnamed-trace messages are non-fatal.

Open PR #112 contains a datasheet-derived LMK1C1104 example and a different package variant, but it does not add a reusable component under `lib/subcircuits`. This PR uses the TSSOP-8 package from the Altium EVM schematic/BOM.

body:
## Summary

- replace all 373 `AM62L32BOGHAANBR` pads' generic 0.30 mm land geometry with TI's AM62L-specific 10 mil (0.254 mm) NSMD land
- add the corresponding 1 mil (0.0254 mm) solder-mask margin, producing TI's 12 mil mask opening
- centralize the geometry in a shared constant and add a focused Circuit JSON regression test for pad count, geometry, identities, and endpoint positions

## Rationale

TI's generic MPBGB03 package drawing shows a 0.30 mm PCB land example and 0.25–0.35 mm component balls. For AM62L escape routing, however, [SPRADI2 Table 3-1](https://www.ti.com/lit/pdf/spradi2) gives a device-specific 10 mil land and 12 mil solder-mask opening. This change uses that exact recommendation: a 0.127 mm pad radius and 0.0254 mm solder-mask margin.

The downstream reproduction previously monkey-patched the package footprint to a 0.25616 mm diameter. That value was derived from the routing equation `0.5 mm pitch - 3 × 0.08128 mm`, not specified by TI, so it is intentionally not upstreamed. TI's documented 0.254 mm land is used instead. See also the [MPBGB03 package drawing](https://www.ti.com/lit/pdf/mpbgb03).

## Validation

- `bun run format:check`
- `bun run typecheck`
- `bun test` — 1 focused test, 373 pads, all at radius 0.127 mm and solder-mask margin 0.0254 mm; pin identities and endpoint positions preserved
- `bunx tsci build lib/chips/AM62L32BOGHAANBR.circuit.tsx` — passed; generated Circuit JSON contains exactly 373 pads with the expected geometry
- `bun run build` — all 117 package circuits built successfully (exit 0)
- linked downstream `ddr-byte1-only` build — all six autorouter phases completed without autorouter errors; U1 has the new 373-pad geometry and U2 is unchanged
- downstream netlist check, layer verification, and shorts check all passed; 11 source nets produced 33 PCB traces and 28 vias

The downstream DRC still reports the same two pre-existing via-to-trace clearance locations near DQ9 and DQ15 (0.006 mm and 0.021 mm versus a 0.05 mm minimum). Those diagnostics were already present with the old monkey patch; they are not shorts, and routing otherwise completes. After this package is released, consumers can remove the React footprint monkey patch and use the component normally.

## Summary

- honor bus `maxLengthSkew` as a hard fanout constraint
- add straight/45-degree meanders after the dense pad escape without changing endpoints or vias
- apply matching atomically to complete normal and grouped-beam route candidates
- reject impossible constraints instead of emitting a skew violation
- validate declared plan lengths, final bus skew, unsupported plane termination, and invalid inputs
- add synthetic and captured AM62L visual regressions

## Why

Core already forwards `maxLengthSkew` into fanout phases, but the solver previously dropped it. This adds a native fanout-aware matcher so the existing one-via escape topology and exact DRC checks remain authoritative.

I evaluated `@tscircuit/length-matching-solver`, but did not add it as a dependency: its current package is unpublished and its public API is differential-pair/HD-route oriented rather than an atomic multi-member fanout-bus API.

## Snapshots

Captured AM62L SOC BYTE1 fanout, matched from 9.611899 mm to 8.499999 mm phase-local skew:

![Length-matched fanout](https://github.com/tscircuit/fanout-solver/blob/feat/fanout-length-matching/tests/__snapshots__/bus-length-matching.snap.svg?raw=1)

title: feat: support schematic sheet graphics
description: Add the schematicgraphic  intrinsic component and emit canonical schematic_graphic Asset records, supporting svgContent, imageUrl, or both, while enforcing SVG standards and improving schematic rendering.
body:
## Summary

- Add the `<schematicgraphic />` intrinsic component and emit canonical `schematic_graphic` Asset records.
- Support `svgContent`, `imageUrl`, or both. `imageUrl` is the canonical Asset source, while `svgContent` is an optional materialized fallback.
- Resolve project/static image paths through the platform while retaining the original `project_relative_path` and storing the resolved, fetchable Asset URL.
- Allow optional positive `width` and `height` props, emitted in schematic units and rendered as centered bounds.
- Keep inline `svgContent` assets Asset-only by default, materialize fetched external SVG content for synchronous rendering, and recover from failed external loads when explicit fallback content exists.
- Enforce canonical-source precedence for valid inline and fetched external assets, restrict `imageUrl` to SVG, and reject malformed inline data assets.
- Preserve first-page stacked-schematic behavior with a focused SVG snapshot and structural page-order coverage.
- Consume the broadened Circuit JSON contract where `asset` and `svg_content` are individually optional but at least one is required; Core deliberately continues emitting a canonical Asset for every prop source.
- Use the released renderer that emits one isolated SVG `<image>` data URL without parsing or rewriting the supplied SVG document.
- Preserve Core's automatic sheet naming/indexing while integrating current main's configurable sheet dimensions; refreshed snapshots now render their actual 500×300 and ANSI-B page sizes.

## Dependencies

- Props: `@tscircuit/props@^0.0.640` (released from merged [tscircuit/props#818](https://github.com/tscircuit/props/pull/818))
- Circuit JSON: `circuit-json@^0.0.479` (released from merged [tscircuit/circuit-json#730](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json/pull/730))
- Renderer: `circuit-to-svg@^0.0.410` (released from merged [tscircuit/circuit-to-svg#695](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-to-svg/pull/695))
- Existing copper-pour preview is inherited unchanged from current `main`: `https://pkg.pr.new/@tscircuit/copper-pour-solver@85`

## Image-tag compatibility

- `svgContent` and SVG files supplied through `imageUrl` must be complete standalone SVG documents, including `xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"` on the root element.
- Browser SVG output keeps the complete document embedded in the image data URL. The committed stacked-schematic SVG snapshot is generated from a `<schematicsheet><schematicgraphic /></schematicsheet>` page-one fixture and contains linked `schematic_sheet`/`schematic_graphic` IDs plus the labeled block diagram in the embedded `href`.
- Tests also decode the emitted `href` and verify exact source content, including labels, source precedence, and page-one placement.
- The current `tsci` schematic-PDF path rasterizes with Resvg. Resvg renders shapes and paths from a nested SVG image but currently omits its `<text>` elements ([resvg#740](https://github.com/linebender/resvg/issues/740)). The SVG snapshot intentionally remains the inspectable source of truth for browser output, while decoded-content assertions protect its labels because the raster snapshot comparator cannot see them; CLI PDF label support needs a separate exporter follow-up.

## Bun 1.4 rationale

The full dependency graph reproducibly fails to resolve the existing copper-pour preview under Bun 1.3.14, while the same graph succeeds under Bun 1.4.0. The sharded test workflow uses Bun 1.4.0, and `vercel.json` uses Vercel's exact-version install command. The copper-pour dependency itself is unchanged from current `main`.

## Validation

- `bunx bun@1.4.0 test` — 1,477 passing, 40 skipped, 0 failing; 58 snapshots
- `bunx bun@1.4.0 test tests/features/schematic-sheet` — 19 passing
- focused nested graphic plus custom-dimension snapshots — 3 passing, 17 assertions
- `bunx bun@1.4.0 run smoke-test:dist`
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bunx bun@1.4.0 run build`
- `git diff origin/main...HEAD --check`
- Biome checks on changed TypeScript and package files
- confirmed installed `circuit-to-svg` is the released `0.0.410`
- confirmed the committed SVG snapshot orders `Sheet 1` → `schematic_graphic`/`image` → `Detailed Schematic` and preserves the exact embedded SVG document

title: feat: render schematic graphic assets
description: Render each schematic graphic as an outer g containing an SVG image hrefdata:imagesvgxml,...; circuit-to-svg no longer parses, injects, sanitizes, or rewrites the source SVG DOM.
body:
## Summary

- render each `schematic_graphic` as an outer `<g>` containing an SVG `<image href="data:image/svg+xml,...">`; circuit-to-svg no longer parses, injects, sanitizes, or rewrites the source SVG DOM
- pass a canonical inline SVG Asset data URL through unchanged, prefer it over `svg_content`, and embed caller-materialized `svg_content` for external Assets
- support `svg_content` without an Asset by encoding its UTF-8 bytes as a base64 SVG data URL
- retain clear errors for missing sources, non-SVG Assets, mismatched or malformed data URLs, raw fragment hashes, misplaced base64 metadata, and external Assets that have not been materialized
- preserve sheet selection and background layering, and center/clamp optional `width` and `height` within the inner-sheet or output viewport
- use each selected sheet's configured dimensions when fitting graphics, including custom-width/custom-height sheets
- rely on the SVG image-document boundary to isolate source CSS, classes, and repeated IDs instead of maintaining a parser/sanitizer dependency chain

## Input requirement

The embedded source must be a complete standalone SVG document. In particular, its root must declare `xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"`; Resvg renders an SVG image without that namespace as blank. circuit-to-svg intentionally does not parse or normalize the document under this architecture.

SVG image mode isolates the source document and disables scripts, interactivity, and external resource loading in browser renderers. Declarative SVG animation may still run when the generated SVG is viewed dynamically in a browser.

## Known CLI/PDF limitation

The current tscircuit CLI schematic-PDF path rasterizes circuit-to-svg output with Resvg 2.6.2. Resvg currently omits `<text>` inside SVG data-URL `<image>` elements ([linebender/resvg#740](https://github.com/linebender/resvg/issues/740)). Shapes render, and the exact text markup remains present in the embedded href, but diagram labels will be absent from CLI-generated schematic PDFs until the rasterizer is changed/fixed or text is converted to paths. Browser SVG rendering is not affected by this Resvg limitation.

The obsolete text visual snapshot was removed instead of being refreshed to a misleading textless image. A machine-visible TODO tracks the Resvg issue, structural tests verify the original text remains embedded, and a separate shape-only pixel test covers the supported Resvg output.

## Validation

- `bun test` — 341 passing, 1 TODO, 0 failing
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bun run build`
- `bun run format:check`
- `git diff --check`
- focused coverage for percent/base64 hrefs, UTF-8 encoding, raw-hash rejection, base64 metadata ordering, Asset precedence, external fallback materialization, missing/invalid sources, sheet scoping, default and custom sheet dimensions, sizing/clamping/centering, layering, opaque parser-invalid content, SVG namespace rendering, source-style isolation, and repeated IDs

Implementation chain:

- props contract: tscircuit/props#818
- Circuit JSON schema: tscircuit/circuit-json#730 / `circuit-json@^0.0.479`
- core follow-up: tscircuit/core#3458

Immutable package preview of the schematic-graphic renderer before the custom-sheet integration: https://pkg.pr.new/circuit-to-svg@c8ef526

title: fix: accept same-net copper at trace endpoints
description: Fixes false disconnected endpoint findings by allowing same-net copper connections at trace endpoints, improving trace continuity checks.
body:
## Stack

- Reproduction/base: #246
- This PR flips the four false disconnected-endpoint findings in that reproduction to zero.

## Root cause

The net-level branch of checkTracesAreContiguous only recognized endpoints touching pads. Region rerouting deliberately returns a replacement trace section whose endpoint copper overlaps retained same-net trace sections, so each valid join was reported as disconnected.

## Fix

- prove contact at the exact endpoint against same-layer trace segments on the same logical net
- use actual round-cap copper widths and a 1e-9 numeric tolerance, not coordinate equality
- keep contact local to the endpoint so a trace touching elsewhere cannot hide a floating end
- index candidates lazily by logical net and layer; fully padded routes pay no new preprocessing
- stay conservative for interpolated traces and vias, whose geometry/layer-span semantics need separate handling

Coverage includes T-junctions, shared source nets, wrong nets/layers, sub-micron near misses, short and closed traces, width changes, zero-length route points, and contact elsewhere along the owner trace.

## Validation

- full test suite: 220 pass, 0 fail

title: Preserve explicit ground connections instead of redundant GND branches
description: Fixes the issue of redundant ground branches in the PGA300 circuit by preserving explicit ground connections and preventing unnecessary routing.
body:
## Context

The PGA300 reproduction from #930 is now merged into `main`. This PR is rebased onto the latest `main` (`5091d2f`) and contains one fix commit.

The global ground spanning tree was replacing the circuit's explicit PGA300 COMP–R1 ground wire with two unnecessary branches: COMP–U1.GND and COMP–C3.

## Fix

- Extend the existing `getGroundConnectionPolicy` path used by both the MSP and long-distance solvers.
- For nets explicitly marked `isGround`, preserve physical islands defined by explicit pin-to-pin traces.
- Treat label-only ground pins as separate physical islands and connect those islands electrically through labels rather than new routed traces.
- Prevent long-distance recovery from recreating the redundant ground branches.
- Keep existing automatic ground-bus behavior for unannotated nets and marked ground nets without explicit wires.
- Avoid circuit-specific pin IDs or coordinates in production code.

The full-circuit regression now requires the explicit COMP–R1 connection, rejects both redundant branches, verifies all source GND pins remain electrically connected through traces and labels, and preserves the vertical Q1–R1 connection.

title: fix(schematic): preserve component field and net label placement
description: Fixes the issue where KiCad rearranges component fields and net labels, ensuring that their positions are preserved as specified in Circuit JSON.
body:
## Summary

- preserves Circuit JSON’s explicit placement for component fields by writing `fields_autoplaced no` for every exported symbol instance;
- preserves net-label anchors by disabling KiCad auto-placement for both regular global labels and label-backed symbols;
- adds a serialization assertion to `repro18` so every affected exported object remains explicitly positioned.

## Root cause

The converter calculated and wrote component-field positions and net-label anchor positions, but then marked the same KiCad objects as `fields_autoplaced`. KiCad treats that flag as permission to rearrange fields when the schematic is opened. That second placement pass can move text away from its Circuit JSON coordinates, causing footprint identifiers and net labels to crowd pins or lose their intended spacing.

## Fix

Set `fields_autoplaced` to `no` for exported schematic symbols and net labels. KiCad now retains the coordinates supplied by Circuit JSON instead of replacing them with automatic placement. This applies to every component symbol and label, not only the minimal fixture used by the reproduction.

## Test plan

- `bun test tests/sch/repros/repro18-footprint-net-label-alignment.test.tsx`
- `bun run typecheck`
- `bun run build`

The local test exercised KiCad 10.0.5 successfully. The snapshot baseline remains the CI-generated Linux baseline so the pull-request workflow remains the final visual verification.

body:
## Summary

Adds a focused visual regression test demonstrating that schematic text placement is not preserved when Circuit JSON is converted to KiCad.

The side-by-side snapshot shows the broader export problem: component fields, including the footprint identifier, and connected net labels are positioned correctly relative to the symbol in Circuit JSON, but appear displaced or inconsistently aligned in the generated KiCad schematic.

This is not specific to the component used in the fixture. The fixture is intentionally small so the mismatch is easy to see, but the same conversion behavior affects component symbols generally. Any schematic containing multiple components can therefore accumulate repeated label and field placement errors after export.

## Motivation

Schematic conversion should preserve readability as well as electrical connectivity. When component fields and net labels shift during export:

- labels can crowd pins, wires, or nearby text;
- footprint identifiers no longer maintain the intended spacing from their symbols;
- larger schematics require repetitive manual repositioning in KiCad;
- regenerated exports can undo that cleanup, making the workflow difficult to maintain;
- visual review becomes less reliable because the KiCad result no longer matches the source schematic layout.

A regression snapshot gives this systemic placement issue a stable, reviewable reproduction and provides a baseline for a follow-up fix without changing converter behavior in this PR.

## Test plan

- `bun test tests/sch/repros/repro18-footprint-net-label-alignment.test.tsx`
- `bunx biome check tests/sch/repros/repro18-footprint-net-label-alignment.test.tsx`

## Reference schematic

[TI TIDA-010266 / TIDUF53, Figure 4-1 (page 17)](https://www.ti.com/lit/ug/tiduf53/tiduf53.pdf#page=17). The relevant stage is **U5 INA350CDSIDSGR + C13**. J10 is an optional gain-selection jumper on the parent board.

![TI TIDA-010266 reference schematic, including INA350CDSIDSGR U5 and C13](https://www.ti.com/ods/images/TIDUF53/GUID-20231204-SS0I-WWGZ-JTG0-ZP5LHS9HJ7WJ-low.svg)

Pinout, gain selection, and shutdown behavior: [INA350 datasheet, Table 6-1](https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/ina350.pdf#page=4).

![INA350CDS reusable module schematic with external REF, GS, and SHDN](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/ti/ca2ff97791e1c3f526762799d79c2b0536a2b0d6/lib/subcircuits/__snapshots__/InstrumentationAmplifier_INA350.circuit-schematic.snap.svg)

The parent provides supply, reference generator, sensor, ADC/filter, and any controls. The example connects named parent nets without physical connectors; routing is disabled there until actual application components terminate the nets. REF is not tied to ground, and SHDN is not pulled low.

- `bun test tests`: **17 passed, 0 failed**.
- `bun run typecheck`: passed.
- Biome formatting check on all nine changed TypeScript files: passed.
- Header-free example CLI build: passed with no circuit error records (parts engine disabled).
- Routed integration tests: external gain control, gain 30, and gain 50; all interface pins connected to test-only parent endpoints.
- Tests verify exactly two module components, CDS/ABS pinouts and footprints, external REF/SHDN isolation, and isolation between two imported modules.
- Refreshed schematic/PCB snapshots and visually reviewed them.

## Notes

Use 1.8–5.5 V supply and meet the datasheet input/common-mode/output limits. Fixed gain 50 uses a bottom-layer gain strap with two vias to preserve SHDN clearance; the module uses 0.1 mm traces and requires final parent-board DRC/fabrication review.

## Summary

- coordinate fixed interstitial dogbone sites across multiple signal buses and dense singleton plane drops
- preserve per-layer winding constraints while trying bounded cross-layer interleavings
- length-match dense fanout prefixes only when the remaining plane dogbones still have a complete legal assignment
- bound route diversity and multi-span meander search to avoid combinatorial growth
- add a captured AM62L SoC phase repro with a focused functional/DRC/SVG regression and an interactive debugger page

This is the solver support needed by the AM62L/LPDDR4 Core regression with two byte buses, an 8-signal address/control bus, 212 plane drops, dogbones, and through-all vias.

## Repro

`tests/am62l-lpddr4-three-bus-through-all-repro.test.ts` exercises the self-contained SoC fanout phase:

- 126 connections and 373 active AM62L BGA pads
- 102 singleton power-plane drops plus three 8-signal boundary buses
- 8 layers, via-in-pad disabled, blind/buried vias disabled
- one full-stack dogbone via per connection
- BYTE0/BYTE1/ADDR_CTRL skew limits of 8/14.5/15 mm

The predecessor did not complete this fixture within a 45-second cutoff. This branch completes it in about 18 seconds locally, validates all 126 traces, and passes independent routed-copper DRC. The same fixture is available interactively at `repros/repro03-am62l-three-bus-through-all.page.tsx`; it does not auto-run.

- Core AM62L/LPDDR4 three-bus integration: 5,045 assertions, ~51.2 s test body / ~52.0 s wall
- isolated phase solves:

  - SoC BYTE0 7.175 mm, BYTE1 14.191 mm, ADDR_CTRL 13.613 mm
  - RAM BYTE0 8.000 mm, BYTE1 14.500 mm, ADDR_CTRL 15.000 mm

The broad suite is left to hosted CI to avoid overloading the development machine after an earlier crash.

## Summary

- assign component-wide legal dogbone via sites before routing dense mixed signal and plane fanouts
- keep route transitions logical while modeling through-all physical barrels when blind and buried vias are disabled
- require explicit SimpleRouteJson allowViaInPad true before using via-in-pad

title: Render schematic hierarchy blocks and sheet entries
description: Renders the native records that make up Altium schematic hierarchy blocks, ensuring they are visible in native source previews and converted previews.
body:
## Summary

Renders the native records that make up Altium schematic hierarchy blocks:

- `RECORD=15`: sheet symbol body
- `RECORD=16`: sheet entry
- `RECORD=32`: sheet name
- `RECORD=33`: sheet filename

AltiumTS already parsed these records, but its SVG serializer skipped them. As a result, hierarchy blocks disappeared from native source previews and converted previews even when the Altium documents were correct.

## Implementation

- Uses each sheet symbol's native position and size.
- Places each owned entry from its native side and distance fields.
- Uses the document font table for sheet text.
- Uses each entry's native `TEXTFONTID` for its label.
- Keeps the hierarchy renderer and font lookup in focused modules instead of expanding the main SVG serializer.
- Uses the existing schematic component palette for hierarchy blocks.

## Why this belongs in AltiumTS

The converter was already writing the hierarchy records correctly. Changing the converter or post-processing its SVG would leave native Altium source previews broken and would hide the actual renderer omission.

This change only renders the four hierarchy record kinds above. It does not alter wire geometry, net connectivity, or record ordering. In particular, the floating blue wire stubs visible in the converter's HERON PAY-SSM snapshot are native `RECORD=27` records from the source schematic; they are not created by this change.

## Verification

- Focused SVG snapshot with one hierarchy block and input/output entries.
- Existing open-source Elk Pi SVG snapshot.

- `bun run lint`
- `bun run typecheck`

body:
## Summary

Preserves native Altium No ERC markers through conversion and makes hierarchy blocks visible in the existing source/converted SVG comparisons.

- Applies the existing `source_port.do_not_connect` property after hierarchical sheet-entry ports have been created.
- Preserves standalone No ERC markers without adding a visible port symbol or changing the Circuit JSON schema.
- Writes sheet-entry No ERC markers at their native Altium positions.
- Pins AltiumTS `main` at `a6ef9bf303f150107b9a83307df67b262c557083`, which contains merged [AltiumTS #68](https://github.com/tscircuit/altiumts/pull/68), to render native sheet symbols, sheet entries, sheet names, and sheet filenames.
- Updates the existing HERON PAY-SSM, HERON Systems, and multi-sheet snapshots through Bun's SVG matcher.

## Why

No ERC records were previously processed before hierarchical sheet entries existed, and standalone markers had no internal representation. PAY-SSM therefore lost all 22 markers, while HERON Systems preserved only 8 of 10.

The missing hierarchy blocks were a separate renderer bug. Both the source and converted Altium documents already contained the records, but AltiumTS did not render:

- `RECORD=15`: sheet symbol
- `RECORD=16`: sheet entry
- `RECORD=32`: sheet name
- `RECORD=33`: sheet filename

This hid 16 sheet symbols and 94 entries in PAY-SSM, and 7 sheet symbols and 34 entries in HERON Systems, on both sides of the comparison.

The converter continues to use the existing `do_not_connect` property, and every output position comes from native Altium geometry. The SVG snapshots are not edited, injected, or transformed.

## Roundtrip 2 wire stubs

The short blue segments around labels such as `A_PHASE_MOT1`, `ADC1_CS_N`, and `PEX_CS` are native top-level Altium wire records (`RECORD=27`) with net labels (`RECORD=25`). They already exist in the HERON PAY-SSM source and are intentionally preserved. They are not missing component bodies and are not introduced by either fix in this PR.

## Verification

- `bun run format:check`
- `bun run typecheck`
- `bun test` — 49 tests passed across 49 files with 541 assertions.
- One focused test file covers standalone No ERC round trips.
- One focused test file covers sheet-entry No ERC placement.
